title: Commit Inspector: recommendation playback, safe-apply gates, and immutable audit log for Optimize
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: deliver a unified UX for Optimize recommendations that lets customers preview batching/caching config changes, run a sandboxed dry-run (playback) to estimate unit-cost and latency impact, and safely apply or rollback changes with an immutable commit inspector. The feature reduces friction for applying cost-saving changes while preserving an audit trail for compliance and post-mortem reconciliation.
background: Customer problem: teams hesitate to apply auto-generated batching/caching recommendations because they lack a reliable way to preview runtime impact and an easy rollback path when regressions are detected.

Scope: recommendation cards + inline diff preview + sandboxed playback (dry-run) + safe-apply workflow with canary window, automatic fallback, and immutable audit entries visible in Console's Optimize timeline.
Related initiatives: runtime-1.20 kernel-selection work, caching-memoization infra, and rollout-engine safe-fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation card shows predicted percentage cost reduction, expected latency delta, confidence band, and primary changed config keys (batch_size, cache_window_seconds, cache_prefix_rules).

Clicking 'Preview diff' opens a side panel that renders the JSON config diff, highlights tokenized risk vectors (e.g., reduced prefix cache TTL), and links example evaluation prompts and quality regressions if present.

Playback (sandbox dry-run) executes simulated traffic for the user's selected route/model for N requests and returns observed token throughput, median latency, and extrapolated monthly savings estimate under their current traffic profile.

Safe-apply workflow presents two options: Live Apply with Canaries (default) and Scheduled Change. Live Apply performs a time-boxed canary rollout with auto-rollback on SLA/regression triggers defined in the policy.

Commit Inspector appends an immutable audit entry for every Preview, Playback, Apply, and Rollback action containing user, timestamp, diff snapshot, playback metrics, and the final outcome. Entries are queryable by route/model and exportable as CSV.
UI includes clear rollback affordances: single-click rollback to last known-good config and an irreversible 'Archive' button for old commits.

End-to-end e2e smoke tests and telemetry: events for preview_open, playback_start/complete, apply_started/complete/failure, rollback_started/complete must be instrumented and available in the Optimize console telemetry dashboard.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: exposing estimated savings increases risk of false positives — we surface confidence bands and link to recent evals to mitigate. Engineering prefers a limited preview dataset for playback to bound cost and latency of dry-runs.
Design request: minimize cognitive load by collapsing low-impact diffs, and surface only config keys with >5% predicted cost impact by default.

Security/compliance: audit entries must be WORM-like for enterprise tenants; gating L1 customers may require KMS-backed immutable storage. Marked that Private deployments might need a different storage target.
Backfill requirement: migration job to populate historical recommendations into new commit-inspector timeline for customers with prior Optimize activity (low priority).
